analysis:
All changes are in test code under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests (fixtures and live tests). None are shipped in the provider binary, so they add no production attack surface and do not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, or the fan helper.

SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift (~line 97): doc-comment change only.

GemmaOpenRouterLiveTests.swift (lines 62-83): the test now aggregates streamed tool-call fragments by wire index instead of appending them. It is local to the test, gated behind live-test env flags, and prints only tool names and the first 100 chars of content, which is already the behavior in base. A nil index falls back to fragments.count, which affects test correctness only.

GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift (line 265): adds a `.toolCallDelta` case to the switch so it stays exhaustive, with Issue.record on that path. This implies a new enum case in the MLXLMServer stream event type outside this batch. Whether that case could leak partial tool-call or plaintext content on the production path is not visible here and is out of scope.

ModelCheckpointStorageSpecificationTests.swift (lines 75-76) and ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift (lines 38-50, from the patch; the full file is not supplied): the fixture environment pins the prefill chunk and step token budget alongside the solo stripe key. The cache-related env keys (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, _TEST_ROOT, _ALLOW_EPHEMERAL) are unchanged, so the T-041 posture is unchanged. Wording such as 'swallow' indicates a scheduler-geometry fix.

Remaining question for integration: the production-side changes (EngineV2Factory prefillChunkKey/stepTokenBudgetKey, the toolCallDelta streaming event) are not in this batch. They should be reviewed in their own batches. In particular, toolCallDelta streaming must be confirmed to stay inside the encrypted response path (T-008).
